title: Alert Triangle Prioritization and Operator Batcher Playbook
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Summary

This playbook defines the "Alert Triangle" prioritization model and the Operator Batcher mechanism we use to reduce noise while preserving timely action for true incidents. It is intended for platform operators, SREs, monitoring engineers, and feature owners who onboard observability signals to the Redwood platform.

Goals

- Reduce actionable alert volume by aggregating low-utility signals without increasing mean time to detect (MTTD) for high-severity incidents.
- Standardize alert contracts so owners can reason about expected operator responses and escalation ladders.
- Provide a reproducible on-call triage and batching process that is automatable and auditable.

Scope

Applies to:
- Platform infrastructure services (ingest, scheduler, batcher, cache, runtime).
- Cross-tenant control plane services (routing, billing, metering).
- Observability stacks (Prometheus, Cortex, Alertmanager, Datadog, Honeycomb).

Excludes: customer application alerts (customer teams own their alerts but are encouraged to adopt this model).

Key Concepts

1) Alert Triangle (visual metaphor)
- Apex (Cut-the-Glass): Critical service outages that directly violate SLOs or create data loss. Immediate page.
- Middle (Actionable): Symptoms likely to degrade SLOs or cause escalations if not remedied within 15–60 minutes. Pager only if trend sustained; otherwise batched.
- Base (Informational / Signal): High-volume, low-immediacy indicators (e.g., small cache misses, single-tenant cold starts). Digitally batched and surfaced to operators as a digest.

2) Operator Batcher
- A lightweight operator-side service (in-platform) that consumes low/mid-priority alerts, groups them into contextual digests, and forwards a single synthesized alert to the operator channel at configurable cadences (default 15 min).
- Supports enrichment with recent traces, top-k affected tenants, and inferred root-cause tags to preserve actionability.

Prioritization Matrix (contract template)

| Triangle Tier | SLO impact window | Expected operator response | Escalation window | Pager? | Batchable? |
|---------------|--------------------|----------------------------|-------------------|--------|------------|
| Cut-the-Glass | Immediate (0–2 min) | Immediate mitigation / rollback | 0–5 min | Yes | No |
| Actionable | Degradation over 15–60 min | Investigate, apply mitigation runbook | 15–60 min | Conditional | Partial (if transient) |
| Informational | >60 min / low severity | Track, create ticket, >= next digest | N/A | No | Yes |

Alert Contract: fields every alert must provide
- service_owner (team id)
- declared_SLO (metric id and threshold)
- detection_query (PromQL/Datadog query snippet)
- symptom_tags (top 3)
- suggested_playbook (link)
- minimum_ttl_seconds (to avoid thrash)
- dedup_key (stable identifier for deduping)

Operator Batcher Design and Configuration

Component responsibilities:
- Ingest: subscribe to Alertmanager webhook and Datadog events stream.
- Classifier: label each alert into Triangle Tier using rules and ML heuristics (default ruleset provided below).
- Aggregator: group alerts by service_owner, symptom_tags, and topology (region/cluster).
- Synthesizer: create digest summary with: count, top-3 traces, most-frequent error messages, top tenants affected, 90/95th percentile latencies for the window.
- Forwarder: post digest to the operators channel and to the ticketing system (Jira) if digest indicates persistent trend.

Default thresholds (configurable per service):
- Batch window: 900s (15m)
- Minimum events to escalate digest as Jira: 50 events across 15m or >5% of tenant requests affected
- Transient suppression TTL: 120s (ignore duplicate alerts with same dedup_key within 120s)
- Escalation backoff: exponential, 1h -> 2h -> 4h cap at 24h

Classifier rules (ordered):
1. If alert dedup_key matches an active Cut-the-Glass page -> Tier Apex.
2. If alert includes SLO_violation=true OR error_rate > SLO_threshold for last 1m -> Tier Apex.
3. If alert's rolling error rate crosses 2x baseline for 15m OR latency p95 > declared threshold for 10m -> Tier Actionable.
4. Else -> Tier Informational.

Sample Alertmanager webhook snippet (recommended format)

POST /operator-batcher/webhook
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "alertname": "cache-miss-spike",
  "service_owner": "runtime-team",
  "dedup_key": "cache:cluster-prod:prefix-23",
  "detected_at": "2026-02-12T14:35:02Z",
  "symptom_tags": ["cache", "miss-ratio", "prefix-evictions"],
  "metrics": {"error_rate_1m": "0.043", "p95_latency_ms": "78"},
  "suggested_playbook": "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/kv-prefix-cache-drain-rolling-deploy-playbook-2026"
}

Runbook: On-call triage (operator flow)

1. Receive page/digest. Immediately validate (first 2 minutes):
   - Check SLO dashboard for the declared SLO.
   - Verify detection query execution (copy/paste PromQL or run Datadog event query).
2. If apex page: follow Cut-the-Glass runbook:
   - Execute fast rollback (if deployment triggered) or promote fallback model.
   - Notify product SLA owner and customer success if customer-facing.
   - Post timeline to incident Slack channel and create incident in PagerDuty + Incident Timeline doc.
3. If actionable:
   - Determine whether immediate manual mitigation (scale up, change routing) is warranted.
   - If mitigation applied, annotate digest with operator action and set check-back timer (15m).
   - If no mitigation, escalate to owner on-call after configured window.
4. If informational digest:
   - Open an investigation ticket if digest persists for 3 consecutive digests.
   - Otherwise, mark as mitigated in digest and continue monitoring.

Operators must always attach the dedup_key to any created Jira ticket; tickets without dedup_key are rejected by the automation.

Dashboards and Alerts to Deploy

Minimum dashboards per service_owner (templates available under /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/templates):
- SLO Overview (SLO burn, current error budget, recent alerts mapped to time)
- Triangle Digest View (live feed of recent digests, top symptoms, action history)
- Alert Volume Heatmap (alerts per 15m by symptom_tags)
- Operator Action Log (actions taken tied to digests / denormalized)

Suggested PromQL / example monitor definitions:
- Error-rate-one-minute: 
  sum(rate(http_request_errors_total[1m])) by (service) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m])) by (service)
- P95-latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, service))

Datadog composite check example (pseudo):
- query: "avg(last_15m):avg:service.request_latency.p95{env:prod,service:runtime} > 120"
- notify: operator-batcher-webhook + runtime-oncall

Escalation Matrix

- Pager (Cut-the-Glass): immediate to SRE primary -> SRE secondary (10m) -> runtime lead -> platform on-call manager.
- Actionable pager: send digest to operator channel; if not acknowledged in 30m escalate to service_owner on-call.
- Informational digest: no page. If triage ticket opened, assignee must respond within 2 business days.

Change and Rollback Procedures for Monitoring Signals

1. To onboard a new alert: submit an "alert contract" PR to observability-config repo. Include detection_query, declared tier, runbook link, and minimum_ttl_seconds.
2. Automated CI verifies query parseability, verifies it references a declared metric, and runs a simulated 1d dry-run against the historic event store.
3. If dry-run shows >2000 pages/day or >20% of historical incidents would be paged, the alert is rejected and must be tuned.
4. Rollback: alerts are versioned in git. To rollback, revert the PR and post to #observability-ops with the revert tag; the Operator Batcher will re-evaluate the pipeline within 5 minutes.

Onboarding checklist for service owners (short)

- [ ] Register service_owner and SLOs in SLO registry.
- [ ] Create alert contract and PR to observability-config.
- [ ] Provide runbook link and playbook steps.
- [ ] Configure batching thresholds (default acceptable).
- [ ] Run 24h simulation and attach runbook with results.
- [ ] Schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with platform SRE.

Measurement and Retrospective

Success metrics (tracked monthly):
- Reduction in unique pages per operator per week (target: -40% within 3 months).
- Mean time to detect for Cut-the-Glass incidents (target: <3m).
- Fraction of actionable incidents batched incorrectly (target: <2%).
- False-positive digest->Jira escalations (target: <5% of escalations).

Retrospective cadence:
- Monthly digest review in the Platform Ops retro. Each retrospective must include two case studies where batching avoided noise and one case where batching delayed detection; corrective actions must be tracked.

Known limitations and caveats

- Operator Batcher relies on quality of dedup_key and symptom_tags. Poorly instrumented services will have lower batching accuracy.
- ML-based classifier is best-effort; deterministic rules are the fallback and source of truth.
- Critical customer-facing product incidents should include an explicit "force-page" bit that bypasses batching.

Ownership and Contacts

- SLO registry contact: slo-admin@redwood.com

Appendix: Example digest payload (synthesized)

{
  "digest_id": "digest-20260215-001",
  "window_secs": 900,
  "tier": "Informational",
  "service_owner": "ingest-team",
  "count": 128,
  "top_symptoms": ["prefetch-failure", "cache-miss"],
  "top_tenants": ["tenant-a", "tenant-x"],
  "p95_latency_ms": "103",
  "suggested_next_step": "investigate kv-prefix eviction policy",
  "ticket_if_escalated": "RED-OBS-1243"
}

(Operator note: the real post uses a JSON attachment; above is for human-readable inclusion in the digest.)

If anything in this playbook is unclear or you need the template files, contact the authors or open a ticket in the observability backlog.
